faq: Are your invoices legally valid in my country?
Invoice rules differ by country. We include the fields you tell us are required, such as a tax number, but we are not tax advisers, so please check requirements with your accountant.
Can you set this up with an invoicing tool like Xero or QuickBooks?
Yes, in many cases through their official connections. Tell us which tool you use, and we confirm what is possible before the work starts.
Will past payments get invoices too?
New payments get them automatically. For older payments, your provider may let us generate documents after the fact. We tell you what is possible before starting.
Can customers add their company details?
In the Premium package, yes. Customers can add a company name and tax ID that then appear on every future invoice, and each invoice keeps a record of what they entered.
desc:
Automatic invoices and receipts for subscriptions, set up by Ecom Swift LLC. After every payment, your customer receives a clean document with your business details and a number you choose, and you do nothing by hand.

## What is the difference between an invoice and a receipt?

An invoice is a document asking for or recording a payment due, with the amount, the items, the dates and the seller and buyer details. A receipt is proof that the payment has been made. For subscriptions, many providers create both, or a single document that serves as each. Which one a customer needs depends on their country and on their accounting team.

Customers rarely look at these documents until they need them. Then they need them immediately and in the right form: a PDF with the company name, the address, a tax number and a clear description of what was bought.

## Why proper invoices save time on both sides

Without automation, someone on your side writes invoices by hand or answers emails asking for them. That work is repetitive, easy to get wrong and always arrives at an inconvenient time. On the customer side, an accountant who cannot find a document may delay payment approval or ask for a corrected one, and this creates friction in a relationship that should be routine.

Documents that arrive automatically, look professional and can be downloaded at any time show that the business is well run. They also reduce support messages and give your own bookkeeper a clean trail. When business buyers can enter their company name and tax ID before paying, the document is correct the first time and no reissue is needed.

## What a good invoicing setup includes

- Automatic invoice creation for every successful payment.
- A receipt email sent right after payment, separate from the invoice email where useful.
- Your business name, address, tax number and logo on the template.
- Invoice numbers with the prefix and sequence you choose.
- A custom footer for payment notes, bank details or legal wording.
- An invoice list inside your app, with a PDF download for each item.
- Fields for the customer's company name and tax ID.
- A copy of each invoice sent to a billing email address.
- Credit note settings checked, so refunds produce the right document.
- A monthly export that your accountant can import or read.

## How we do the work

We begin with your provider's invoice settings, since most already generate documents and only need to be configured properly. The Basic package turns on automatic invoices and receipts, adds your details and logo, and checks a test payment from start to finish. The Standard package sets your numbering and footer, adds an invoice list with PDF downloads in your app, separates receipt and invoice emails and reviews credit note settings. The Premium package adds company and tax ID fields for customers, copies to a billing email, a monthly accountant export, rewritten invoice email wording and handover notes.

We check each document by reading it as a customer and as an accountant would: are the amounts, dates and tax lines clear, and does the numbering run in order? Ecom Swift LLC does not give legal or tax advice, so your accountant should confirm which wording and fields your country requires.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Put your full legal business name and address on every invoice.
- Let customers add company details before the first payment.
- Keep numbering in one unbroken sequence.
- Send a copy to a billing contact when the buyer is a company.
- Ask your accountant which fields your country requires.

**Avoid:**
- Editing invoices by hand after they have been sent.
- Sending a receipt that omits the plan name or billing period.
- Changing your invoice prefix in the middle of a year without a reason.
- Hiding past invoices behind a support request.
- Assuming that one template fits every country you sell in.

## Who this suits

This service suits a SaaS owner who still writes invoices manually after each payment. It suits a company selling to other businesses, whose customers need a tax ID on every document. It also suits a founder preparing for a first accountant or audit who wants a clean record of every sale.

## What we need and how to begin

Send your legal business name, address, tax number if you have one, logo and preferred invoice prefix. Tell us which payment provider you use and whether you also use accounting software. We need developer or collaborator access to your app and a team role in your provider account, and never any passwords. Once you order, we reply with a short checklist and share a sample document for your approval.
